6. # NixOS Configuration Guidelines
7. 
8. ## Deployment Workflow
9. 
10. 1. Edit host config under `anywhere/hosts/<hostname>/configuration.nix`
11. 2. Validate: `nix flake check`
12. 3. Deploy: `nix develop -c deploy .#<hostname>`
13. 
14. **Never use `nixos-anywhere`** for routine changes — it wipes and reinstalls the host.
15. 
16. ## Host File Layout
17. 
18. Each host has: `configuration.nix` (main config), `disko-config.nix` (disk layout), `sops.nix` (secret declarations). The ARM host also has `hardware-configuration.nix`.
19. 
20. ## Secrets
21. 
22. - Encrypted with SOPS + age under `anywhere/secrets/`
23. - Decrypted at activation into `/run/secrets/<name>`
24. - Host age keys live at `/var/lib/sops-nix/key.txt`
25. - Shared secrets: `tailscale/auth-key.yaml`, `k3s/token.yaml`
26. 
27. ## Build Constraints
28. 
29. - All four Oracle micro nodes use deploy-rs `remoteBuild = false`; Mac-initiated deployments build their `x86_64-linux` closures through the hp348 distributed builder.
30. - `oracle-eu-arm1` and `oracle-in-arm1` (aarch64): `remoteBuild = true` — build on the hosts themselves.
31. - `s145`, `hp348`, and `rpi`: `remoteBuild = true`.
32. - The hp348 builder receives the Mac's local flake inputs through Nix; no repository checkout or synchronization is required on hp348.
33. 
34. ## k3s Cluster
35. 
36. - Flannel traffic over `tailscale0` interface
37. - Workers tainted `tiny=true:NoSchedule` with `max-pods=10`
38. - Services conditionally enabled via `builtins.pathExists` on secrets files
